description: Tracks the average price of a fixed basket of goods and services bought by urban consumers.
why_it_matters: The headline U.S. inflation gauge. Month-over-month or year-over-year % change is what people mean by "inflation," and it drives Fed policy decisions.

description: Percent of the labor force that is jobless and actively seeking work.
why_it_matters: Core measure of labor-market health; a rising rate is one of the clearest recession signals.

description: The interest rate depository institutions charge each other for overnight loans.
why_it_matters: The Fed's primary policy lever. Changes here ripple through borrowing costs across the whole economy.

description: Market interest rate on 10-year U.S. government debt.
why_it_matters: Benchmark for mortgage rates and corporate borrowing; reflects long-run growth and inflation expectations.

description: Market interest rate on 2-year U.S. government debt.
why_it_matters: Reflects near-term expectations for Fed policy moves.

description: DGS10 minus DGS2 — the slope of the yield curve.
why_it_matters: A negative spread ("inverted yield curve") is historically one of the most reliable recession predictors.

description: Total dollar value of all goods and services produced in the U.S.
why_it_matters: The broadest single measure of economic output and growth.

indicator_name: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment Index
description: Survey-based measure of how optimistic or pessimistic consumers feel about the economy and their own finances.
why_it_matters: A leading indicator for consumer spending, which drives most of U.S. GDP.
